changes: Removed Paṃkeśa from persons. A Licchavi name ending in -īśa/-eśa (Paṃka + īśa) is almost certainly a Śiva liṅga named after its founder, so it is a deity, not a person; the founder's name may be Paṃka, but the text does not say so.

Changed purpose from 'water conduit' to 'fragmentary; probably concerns the liṅga Paṃkeśa'. Puṇyādhāre most likely means 'on an auspicious occasion', not a reservoir, and nothing in the text points to a water conduit.
place.as_written now gives the full find-spot: 'Lalitpur, Su-bahāla'.
Date: as_written now keeps the full wording 'saṃvat 187 māghaśukladivā 5'.

purpose: Fragment; probably records a pious act (perhaps an endowment) for the liṅga Paṃkeśa. The text breaks off.
notes: Only line 1 survives, and it breaks off. The editor says only 'mentioned śrī-Paṃkeśa' (DV 175). Paṃkeśa looks like the name of a Śiva liṅga (founder's name + īśa, as in Licchavi usage), so it is not listed as a person. The founder (Paṃka?) is not named outright. 'jareṃ' is unclear, possibly corrupt or the start of a lost word. 'puṇyādhāre' is read as 'on an auspicious occasion'. The year is in the Licchavi saṃvat, left unconverted as instructed.
